question.text: A higher Sharpe ratio in relation to another portfolio means:

answer.text: Higher reward per unit of TOTAL risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Sharpe measures reward-to-total-risk; higher = better risk-adjusted performance. The Trap: Other interpretations misread the ratio. Cross-Exam Context: Same in X-B. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Use Sharpe as the default comparator for mutually exclusive portfolios.
